issues.legal_issue: A government lessee remains in occupation of a building when it permits another person to reside there without granting a sublease.
material_facts: The Central Government had taken the portion of the building on lease and used it for a public purpose.
The Government permitted a military officer to reside in the building.
The officer was not occupying the building as a sublessee of the Government.
The dispute arose in an appeal concerning exemption from property tax.
issues.conclusion: The building was in the occupation of the Central Government through the military officer it had permitted to reside there.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 99(2)(f) of the Cantonments Act, 1924, exemption requires that the property be used or acquired for public service or a public purpose and be either State property or in the occupation of the Central or a State Government. Sections 5 to 7 of the Cantonments (House Accommodation) Act, 1923 provide for appropriation by lease to the Central Government. A government lessee that permits another person to reside in the building remains in occupation through that person; the position may differ where the Government grants a sublease. Section 65's reference to actual occupation concerns the primary liability for tax and does not alter this interpretation. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: property_tax_exemption_dispute and government_held_right_to_occupy and government_permitted_resident and resident_was_not_sublessee and property_used_for_public_purpose

predicates.property_tax_exemption_dispute: The proceeding concerned whether property was exempt from property tax.
predicates.government_held_right_to_occupy: The Government held a right to occupy the property, including as a lessee.
predicates.government_permitted_resident: The Government permitted another person to reside in the property.
predicates.resident_was_not_sublessee: The resident occupied the property by permission rather than under a sublease from the Government.
predicates.property_used_for_public_purpose: The property was used for a public purpose.
predicates.government_occupies_through_permitted_re: The Government is treated as occupying the property through the person it permitted to reside there.

issues.definition: When a property-tax exemption dispute concerns property used for a public purpose, and the Government holds a right to occupy it and permits a person who is not its sublessee to reside there, the Government occupies it through that resident.
